title: Finitely many isolated fibre points become finite pieces after an elementary etale base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $s\in S$, and let $x_1,\dots,x_n\in X$ be points with $f(x_i)=s$ each of which is an isolated point of the fibre $X_s=X\times_S\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Then there are a scheme $U$, an etale morphism $\varphi:U\to S$ [def-weil-etale-morphism] and a point $u\in U$ with $\varphi(u)=s$ such that the map $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)$ induced by $\varphi$ on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] is an isomorphism (an elementary etale neighbourhood of $(S,s)$), and open subschemes $V_1,\dots,V_n$ of $X_U=X\times_SU$ [def-pc-fibre-product] such that for each $i$: (i) the composite $V_i\hookrightarrow X_U\to U$ of the inclusion and the second projection is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; (ii) there is exactly one point $v_i\in V_i$ mapping to $u$; (iii) the first projection $X_U\to X$ maps $v_i$ to $x_i$, and the induced map of residue fields $\kappa(x_i)\to\kappa(v_i)$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LL (more-morphisms-lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-multiple-points, line 11974), statement and proof (lines 11974-12011; induction on n from Lemma 02LK, more-morphisms-lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-at-point, line 11924, itself reduced to Algebra, Lemma 00UJ)

proof.text: Induction on $n$, base case $n=0$ (Stacks: 'We will use induction on $n$'; the base case is left implicit there and written out by the agent). For $n=0$ take $U=S$, $\varphi=\mathrm{id}_S$ and $u=s$: the identity is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], hence etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1) [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)$ is the identity of $\kappa(s)$ [def-weil-residue-field]; there are no $V_i$ to choose. For the induction step let $n\ge1$ and suppose that an etale $\varphi:U\to S$, a point $u\in U$ with $\varphi(u)=s$ and $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)$ an isomorphism, and open subschemes $V_1,\dots,V_{n-1}$ of $X_U=X\times_SU$ (projections $p:X_U\to X$, $q:X_U\to U$) satisfying (i)-(iii) for $x_1,\dots,x_{n-1}$ are given (the statement for $x_1,\dots,x_{n-1}$).

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LL (more-morphisms-lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-multiple-points), proof, lines 11998-12011

proof.text: Lift the last point x to X_U directly using canonical field-spectrum maps. Write beta for the isomorphism kappa(phi(t)) -> kappa(t) and alpha for kappa(phi(t)) -> kappa(x), with the residue-field congruence from f(x)=phi(t). The map Spec(kappa(x)) -> U induced by beta inverse followed by alpha commutes over S with the canonical point map into X, by residue-field-point naturality. The pullback universal property gives l:Spec(kappa(x))->X_U. Its unique point z projects to x and t. Factor l through Spec(kappa(z)) using the morphism-from-spec-field theorem. Naturality, the equality of the first projection with the canonical point map, full faithfulness of Spec, and the monomorphism of the canonical point map show that the induced map c:kappa(x)->kappa(z) has a left inverse b:kappa(z)->kappa(x). Since b is an injective field map and split surjective, b and hence c are isomorphisms. No uniqueness of z is needed for the induction.

proof.text: Hypotheses of the one-point case for $x'_n$ (Stacks: 'Also $x'_n$ is isolated in $X_u$'). The second projection $q:X_U\to U$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change], and $q(x'_n)=u$. Since $p(x'_n)=x_n$ is an isolated point of $X_s$, [lem-weil-pbc-isolated-fibre-point-base-change] (with $g=\varphi$) shows that $x'_n$ is an isolated point of the fibre $(X_U)_u$ of $q$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre].

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LL (more-morphisms-lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-multiple-points), proof, lines 11998-12011

proof.text: Application of the one-point case (Stacks: 'Hence by Lemma 02LK there exists an elementary etale neighbourhood $(U',u')\to(U,u)$ and an open $V_n\subset X_{U'}$ which works for $x'_n$'). By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-finite-at-point-elementary] applied to $q:X_U\to U$ and $x'_n$ there are an etale $\psi:U'\to U$, a point $u'\in U'$ with $\psi(u')=u$ and $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(u')$ an isomorphism, and an open subscheme $V_n$ of $X_U\times_UU'$ (projections $\pi:X_U\times_UU'\to X_U$, $q':X_U\times_UU'\to U'$) finite over $U'$, with exactly one point $v_n$ over $u'$, such that $\pi(v_n)=x'_n$ and $\kappa(x'_n)\to\kappa(v_n)$ is an isomorphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. By [lem-weil-pbc-cartesian-square-pasting] (lower square $X_U\to X$ over $\varphi$, upper square $\pi$ over $\psi$), $X_U\times_UU'$ with $p'=p\circ\pi$ and $q'$ is a fibre product $X_{U'}=X\times_SU'$ of $f$ and $\varphi\circ\psi$ [def-pc-fibre-product], and $\pi$ is the morphism with $p\circ\pi=p'$, $q\circ\pi=\psi\circ q'$. The composite $\varphi\circ\psi$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2) [def-weil-etale-morphism], maps $u'$ to $s$, and $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u')$ is the composite of the isomorphisms $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(u)\to\kappa(u')$ [def-weil-residue-field]: $(U',u')$ with $\varphi\circ\psi$ is an elementary etale neighbourhood of $(S,s)$; it is the one of the statement.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LL (more-morphisms-lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-multiple-points), proof, lines 11998-12011

proof.text: $V_n$ works for $x_n$ (Stacks: '... which works for $x'_n$ and hence for $x_n$'; written out by the agent). Properties (i) and (ii) for $V_n\subseteq X_{U'}$ and $u'$ are those of the previous step. For (iii): $p'(v_n)=p(\pi(v_n))=p(x'_n)=x_n$, and the map $\kappa(x_n)\to\kappa(v_n)$ induced by $p'=p\circ\pi$ is the composite of $\kappa(x_n)\to\kappa(x'_n)$ (an isomorphism by step 2) and $\kappa(x'_n)\to\kappa(v_n)$ (an isomorphism by step 4) [def-weil-residue-field], hence an isomorphism.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 02LL (more-morphisms-lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite-multiple-points), proof, lines 11998-12011

proof.text: The earlier opens still work (Stacks: 'By the final assertion of Lemma 02LK the open subschemes $V'_i=U'\times_UV_i$ for $i=1,\dots,n-1$ still work with respect to $x_1,\dots,x_{n-1}$. Hence we win.'). For $i<n$ put $V'_i=\pi^{-1}(V_i)$, an open subscheme of $X_{U'}$. Since $V_i$ satisfies (i)-(iii) for $x_i$ with respect to $(U,u)$ and $\kappa(u)\to\kappa(u')$ is an isomorphism, [lem-weil-pbc-elementary-etale-finite-piece-persistence] (with $\varphi$, $\psi$, $\pi$, $p'$, $q'$ as in step 4) gives that $V'_i\to U'$ is finite, that $V'_i$ has exactly one point $v'_i$ over $u'$, and that $p'(v'_i)=x_i$ with $\kappa(x_i)\to\kappa(v'_i)$ an isomorphism. Together with step 5, the elementary etale neighbourhood $(U',u')$ of step 4 and the opens $V'_1,\dots,V'_{n-1},V_n$ of $X_{U'}$ satisfy (i)-(iii) for $x_1,\dots,x_n$, which completes the induction.
